title: Pinch a pot from air-dry clay
how: Push your thumb into a ball of clay and turn it slowly. It's the oldest way there is to make a pot.
first_step: Roll a ball of clay about the size of a satsuma.
moment_prompt: Your pinch pot, wobbles and all.

title: Practise with kitchen playdough
how: Flour, salt and water make a dough that behaves enough like clay to learn pinching and coiling for free.
first_step: Mix two cups of flour, one cup of salt and water until it holds.

title: Coil a little planter
how: Roll snakes of clay, stack them in rings and smooth the inside. Plant something small once it's dry.
first_step: Roll one even snake about as thick as a pencil.
moment_prompt: The planter with something growing in it.

title: Paint pots with a friend
how: Swap your dried pots and paint each other's. Tea is mandatory.
first_step: Text one friend and pick an evening.

title: Try the wheel at a drop-in class
how: Most studios run taster sessions. Expect to collapse a few. Everyone does.
first_step: Look up a beginner wheel taster near you.
moment_prompt: Your first thing off the wheel.

title: Watch a potter throw, slowly
how: Find a long throwing video with no talking and just watch the hands. It teaches more than you'd think.
first_step: Search for a quiet wheel-throwing video and make tea.
